column6: rationale -- scripts/gen-membudget.py; docs/SIZING.md "Memory budgets"; CONTRIBUTING.md "Memory budgets" for flipping an open row.

an aggregate scan that can spill: its group table (held to hash memory at the end of each unit; a process of a scan with workers holds at most group_par_factor (2) times hash memory, past which the statement runs again as PostgreSQL plans it), the results of the finished table, the caches of the values of its expressions (4 MB at most), the table of an IN list (half of hash memory at most), the state of the partitions of the scan (8 kB each, 2,048 at the default work_mem) and one superblock of write buffer rows (6 MB for 1 kB rows); the rows a scan reads again from the heap hold one whole document as SQL does, which is the size of the document, not of the table (shred_elems)

the groups of an aggregate scan that cannot spill (a top-N or an order on a key that is not an integer, a date or a timestamp, ordered-set aggregates, grouping sets, a two level aggregate, an ungrouped aggregate): the table grows to the bound of the planner, group_nospill_factor (32) times the larger of hash memory and 8 MB, and ends the scan past it (3.5 MB for 5 groups of a percentile)
the table of a lookup join, hashed by key: 22.8 MB measured, it follows the rows of the dimension table (slope row lookup_join_label)
the inverted buffer of a CREATE INDEX of a search index, its runs and the page of text (9.5 MB held at maintenance_work_mem 1MB: 13.6 MB)
the runs and the inverted buffer of a merge of search segments
the sort of the documents of a sealed segment

the state of a search scan: each open segment holds about 165 kB (a 64 kB dictionary block, its header and stream reader), up to 128 segments (24 MB), plus 8 MB of cursors, candidates and top-N; 0.5 MB at 2 segments, 9.8 MB at 60
the walk of one segment and the heap check of sift.verify: a context for each segment, deleted at its end (before: 115 MB held for 60 segments, now 0.2 MB)

the rows, runs and segment writer of CREATE INDEX of a sift_col index: 77 MB held at 4 MB of maintenance_work_mem on 400,000 rows (col_build_memory) and 136 MB at the default; the intended budget is maintenance_work_mem plus a constant, which the build still exceeds: open

the walk over the journal records of the tombstone log of an index (the changed keys of a scope or a connected parent): one block of a run and the blocks of its context, whatever the number of records; the table of the distinct keys, which the read refuses past its cap, is the result's and is not in the scope

the sample and the model of the automatic key_cut of CREATE INDEX, REINDEX and sift.key_cut_decision, which maintenance_work_mem does not bound (a rewrite decides the same key whatever it is): the rows of at most 256 superblocks and 17 units of 74,496 rows (the sample ends at 400,000 rows, and not before 16 superblocks), each 84 bytes with 10 for each leaf (8 at most) and 32 for each key candidate (8 at most), 420 bytes a row at the most, and 1.8 MB besides: 534 MB at the most, whatever the rows of the table; test col_key_cut_sample_small asserts the formula on the exact bytes of the context at 13 sizes on 8-page superblocks

the input segments, one unit of rows of each, and the partition being written by a column merge: 12 to 14 MB at the default maintenance_work_mem on small tables, 36 to 47 MB on 1,600,000 rows at 1 and 4 MB (merge_flatcut), 177 MB in a parallel worker of a key_cut build of 1,600,000 rows at the default maintenance_work_mem ("sift_col merge" holds 154 MB); the intended budget is maintenance_work_mem plus a constant

the decoded units of the inputs of a column merge, the batch they are folded into and the segments open: 9.4 MB at 1 MB of maintenance_work_mem for 12 inputs of 17,000 rows (13.9 MB before the units were given back as they were written), 10.2 MB for 48
the decoded unit of the sweep of overflow records (4.7 MB)
the view of the segments the rewrite rule judges (1 kB)

the answers a scope fill remembers of its btree probes (a member and its keys): forgotten at the next batch once they pass a quarter of maintenance_work_mem, and a batch holds its own (3 pairs a row of 200,000 rows, kept to 262,144 members: 8 MB of members, 10 MB of keys; kept to the quarter: 0.5 MB at 1 MB)

the units decoded and the sorted runs of a scope refill: the sort holds 16 MB at least (23 to 30 MB measured at 1 to 5 MB of maintenance_work_mem in col_build_memory, 47 MB at 1 MB for a scoped concurrent build of 200,000 rows, 52 to 74 MB at the default: a TupleSort of 33 MB, the segment being written 30 MB); the intended budget is maintenance_work_mem plus a constant

the entries a backend caches of the tombstone log of an index, for a scan, VACUUM or the fold of the marks: kept to sift.tomb_log_limit, the rest in sorted runs on temp files; a writer and a read of the header (completeness, key journal) cache none (a scoped concurrent build of 200,000 rows cached 600,000 entries, 32 MB, to read a header)
the two sorts and the window of row hashes of sift.col_verify, each held to maintenance_work_mem (24 MB at the default, 17.6 MB at 4 MB)

the reader of the write buffer of a column index: it copies the records of the buffer to sort them by key, each at its size, and holds one entry of 40 bytes a row: 12.6 MB at the default buffer, up to 93 MB in the crash test of the buffer (col_wbuf_crash: a 512 kB buffer whose open segment holds up to 94,000 rows of 0.9 kB when its seal lags behind eight appenders; 141 MB when the copies were one buffer that doubled); the intended budget is work_mem plus a constant, which a buffer past its limit exceeds: open

the blocks of the order arrays a segment writer builds when its last unit is in (col/spool.h, col/gorder.c): the entries still held, a reader block of 8 kB for each of the at most 64 runs a leaf merges, the directory and the string table of each block built

the entries of the order arrays a segment writer holds until its last unit is in (col/spool.h): a buffer of SIFT_ESET_ROWS entries (256 kB) for each leaf and each of its two regions, the file buffers and the runs of the levels of a leaf that spilled, the blocks built and the merge in hand: the writer weighs the arrays as they would be in memory (16 bytes an entry), a segment is cut at that weight, so what it holds is under its budget
the directory snapshot and the steps of the ambulkdelete and amvacuumcleanup of an index, with the promotions and merges the cleanup runs inside it (8.6 MB at the default maintenance_work_mem)
what one step of the maintenance worker holds besides its promotion or merge, once they end (0.16 MB measured)
the segment read of a value store usage count, reset at each segment (88 kB)
